If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 1.5–2.5% for mid horizon (8–15 days) to compensate for bearish bias.  
When sentiment swings from positive to negative over 3 consecutive days, reduce forecast by 2–3% in late horizon (16–30 days) to reflect reversal risk.  
If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and forecast is trending upward, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% in mid horizon to avoid momentum overfitting.  
If sentiment is neutral and forecast is trending downward, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% in late horizon to offset pessimism.  
If sentiment is consistently high (≥0.8) and forecast is above 80, reduce forecast by 1–2% in late horizon to prevent overcorrection.
